"""
Durable chatbot memory, stored in the conversation history database.

Each memory is one row in ``memories``, in the
same database as chat history.

Memories are per-user. Each agent (including the general global chat agent)
has its own memories. There are three kinds:

- ``user``: a fact or preference about the person, with no metadata link.
  For example, that they like to be called Jamie instead of James. Also known as "about you" memories.
  This type of memory is per-user, per-agent. This means it is not automatically shared across agents.
- ``user-metadata``: a personal preference about specific metadata, linked
  to at least one view, database, or tag. For example, that Jamie likes
  the field salary in samples_bank.loan to always show the currency sign.
  This type of memory is per-user, per-agent. This means it is not automatically shared across agents.
  The same preference with no link would be a ``user`` memory. Also known as "data preferences" memories.
- ``metadata``: an objective fact about the metadata that is not in the
  metadata itself, linked to at least one view, database, or tag. For
  example, that the currency of salary in samples_bank.loan is USD.
  This type of memory is per-user and shared across all agents.
  One name is one fact: a write from any agent replaces that fact.

``user`` and ``user-metadata`` memories belong to one agent. A specialized
agent can also see the general agent's ``user`` and ``user-metadata``
memories when its YAML sets ``share_general_memory`` (on by default).
A write or delete then updates that shared row, unless this agent already
has its own memory of the same name.

A memory name is unique for one user. ``prefers-eur`` cannot be saved again
as another type, or on another agent. A write may only replace the row it
already owns: this agent's row, the general agent's row when sharing is on
and this agent has no row of its own, or the one metadata fact of that name.
Any other row with that name is left in place and the write is refused.

The ``user`` memories index is loaded into the system prompt. Only the first 200
lines are loaded. ``user-metadata`` and ``metadata`` have no such cap because they are
attached to ``metadata_search`` results, only when a linked view, database,
or tag appears in those results.
"""

import json
import re
import logging
import threading
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import yaml

from utils.database_utils import UserMemories

MAX_NAME_LENGTH = 64
MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH = 1024
MAX_BODY_LENGTH = 100000
MAX_LINK_NAME_LENGTH = 256
MAX_LINKS = 100

# The user-memory index loaded into the system prompt is capped at 200
# lines. A write near that cap asks the agent to shorten the index. A
# write past it still succeeds.
MAX_INDEX_LINES = 200
NEAR_INDEX_LINES = 180

MEMORY_TYPES = ("user", "user-metadata", "metadata")
GLOBAL_AGENT_ID = "global"
# Kinds a specialized agent may inherit from the general agent.
# 'metadata' is not in this list: it belongs to the user and every agent
# of that user can read it.
SHARED_MEMORY_TYPES = ("user", "user-metadata")
LINKED_MEMORY_TYPES = ("user-metadata", "metadata")
LINK_KINDS = ("view", "database", "tag")
_LINK_SUFFIX = {"view": "views", "database": "databases", "tag": "tags"}

class _Quoted(str):
    """String value that is dumped in double quotes. Keys stay plain."""

class _QuotedDumper(yaml.SafeDumper):
    """Dumper that honors ``_Quoted`` values."""

def _represent_quoted(dumper, data):
    return dumper.represent_scalar("tag:yaml.org,2002:str", str(data), style='"')

_QuotedDumper.add_representer(_Quoted, _represent_quoted)

def _q(value):
    return _Quoted(value)

_NAME_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$")
_MEMORIES_BLOCK = re.compile(r"<memories>.*?</memories>", re.DOTALL)
_PROMPT_MEMORY_BLOCK = re.compile(
    r"\n*<memory>\s*Durable memory persists.*?</memory>\s*",
    re.DOTALL,
)
_MEMORY_TOOL_LINE = (
    "Facts that should persist across sessions belong in memory. "
    "Read and write those with the memory tools."
)

_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
_user_locks = {}
_store_lock = threading.Lock()
_store_ready = False

class MemoryError(Exception):
    """Raised when a memory cannot be read or written."""

def ensure_memory_store():
    """Create the memory tables in the conversation history database."""
    global _store_ready
    with _store_lock:
        if _store_ready:
            return
        UserMemories.init_db()
        _store_ready = True

def _agent_id(agent_id):
    agent_id = str(agent_id or "").strip()
    return agent_id or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID

def _visible_agent_ids(agent_id, include_shared_general=False):
    """Agents whose user/user-metadata memories this agent may read, own first."""
    agent_id = _agent_id(agent_id)
    if include_shared_general and agent_id != GLOBAL_AGENT_ID:
        return [agent_id, GLOBAL_AGENT_ID]
    return [agent_id]

def _load_visible(username, memory_type, agent_id, include_shared_general=False):
    """Entries of one kind visible to an agent.

    ``user`` and ``user-metadata`` stay on one agent, plus the general
    agent's copies when sharing is on. The agent's own copy wins a name
    clash. ``metadata`` is per user: every agent sees every metadata memory
    that user has saved, whichever agent saved it.
    """
    if memory_type == "metadata":
        return _load_metadata(username, agent_id)
    if memory_type in SHARED_MEMORY_TYPES:
        scopes = _visible_agent_ids(agent_id, include_shared_general)
    else:
        scopes = [_agent_id(agent_id)]
    records = []
    seen = set()
    for scope in scopes:
        for record in _load_entries(username, memory_type, scope):
            if record["name"] in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(record["name"])
            records.append(record)
    return records

def _all_metadata(username):
    """Every metadata row this user has, including duplicate names."""
    username = _validate_username(username)
    ensure_memory_store()
    return [
        _record_from_stored(row)
        for row in UserMemories.list_type_for_user(username, "metadata")
    ]

def _metadata_named(username, name):
    """Every copy of one metadata name. A user should have only one."""
    return [record for record in _all_metadata(username) if record["name"] == name]

def _rows_named(username, name):
    """Every memory this user has under this name, any type, any agent."""
    found = []
    for memory_type in MEMORY_TYPES:
        for row in UserMemories.list_type_for_user(username, memory_type):
            if row["name"] == name:
                found.append(_record_from_stored(row))
    return found

def _name_conflict(username, name, memory_type, target_agent):
    """A different memory that already uses this name, or None.

    The row this write replaces is not a conflict. Every metadata copy of
    this same name is that one fact, so those copies are not a conflict
    either. The write deletes the spare copies.
    """
    target_agent = _agent_id(target_agent)
    for record in _rows_named(username, name):
        if memory_type == "metadata" and record["type"] == "metadata":
            continue
        agent = record.get("agent_id") or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID
        if record["type"] == memory_type and agent == target_agent:
            continue
        return record
    return None

def _name_taken_message(record, name):
    return (
        f"A {record['type']} memory named '{name}' already exists. "
        "Delete it or choose another name."
    )

def _shared_general_memory(username, memory_type, name, agent_id, include_shared_general):
    """The general agent's row of this name, when this agent may change it.

    Used only when this agent has no row of its own. Sharing off, or a call
    on the general agent itself, returns None.
    """
    if memory_type not in SHARED_MEMORY_TYPES:
        return None
    if not include_shared_general or agent_id == GLOBAL_AGENT_ID:
        return None
    for record in _load_entries(username, memory_type, GLOBAL_AGENT_ID):
        if record["name"] == name:
            return record
    return None

def _preferred_metadata(copies, agent_id):
    """The copy a write or a read should keep. The current agent wins a tie."""
    agent_id = _agent_id(agent_id)
    for record in copies:
        if (record.get("agent_id") or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID) == agent_id:
            return record
    return copies[0] if copies else None

def _load_metadata(username, agent_id):
    """One metadata memory per name for this user, current agent first.

    An older duplicate name is hidden. The next write of that name drops it.
    """
    prefer = _agent_id(agent_id)
    records = _all_metadata(username)
    records.sort(key=lambda record: (
        0 if (record.get("agent_id") or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID) == prefer else 1,
        record.get("name") or "",
    ))
    unique = []
    seen = set()
    for record in records:
        if record["name"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(record["name"])
        unique.append(record)
    return unique

def render_user_memories_content(username, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Index text of this user's 'user' memories, without the wrapper tags.

    This fills the ``{memories}`` placeholder of the system prompt when the
    engine is built, so it is fixed for the life of that engine. Only
    link-free ``user`` memories are listed. ``user-metadata`` and
    ``metadata`` memories surface through ``metadata_search`` instead.
    """
    try:
        records = _load_visible(username, "user", agent_id, include_shared_general)
    except MemoryError:
        logging.warning("Skipping user memories for an invalid username.")
        records = []
    kept, truncated = _truncate_index(_index_text(records))
    lines = []
    if kept:
        lines.append("\n".join(kept))
    if truncated:
        lines.append(
            "The memories index is over the 200-line limit, so later lines were left out. "
            "Rewrite it by merging or dropping stale memories next time you deal with memories."
        )
    return "\n".join(line for line in lines if line)

def render_user_memories_block(username, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Index of this user's 'user' memories, wrapped in ``<memories>`` tags."""
    inner = render_user_memories_content(username, agent_id, include_shared_general)
    if inner:
        return f"<memories>\n{inner}\n</memories>"
    return "<memories>\n</memories>"

def is_memory_enabled(username, agent_id):
    """Whether this agent should form and use memories for this user.

    Missing preference means on.
    """
    ensure_memory_store()
    return UserMemories.is_enabled(username, agent_id or "global")

def set_memory_enabled(username, agent_id, enabled):
    """Turn memory formation on or off for one user on one agent."""
    ensure_memory_store()
    UserMemories.set_enabled(username, agent_id or "global", bool(enabled))

def strip_memory_prompt(system_text):
    """Remove the memory instructions and the memory index placeholder.

    Used when memory formation is off for this agent. A ``<memories>``
    fragment inside custom instructions is left alone, because the
    placeholder owned by the chatbot prompt is the last block.
    """
    if not system_text:
        return system_text
    text = _PROMPT_MEMORY_BLOCK.sub("\n\n", system_text)
    matches = list(_MEMORIES_BLOCK.finditer(text))
    if matches:
        match = matches[-1]
        text = text[:match.start()] + text[match.end():]
    text = text.replace(_MEMORY_TOOL_LINE, "")
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text)

def render_metadata_memories_section(username, agent_id, response, include_shared_general=False):
    """Index lines for linked memories that match a ``metadata_search``.

    Covers this agent's ``user-metadata`` and ``metadata`` memories, plus
    the general agent's ``user-metadata`` ones when sharing is on. Nothing
    is attached unless a linked view, database, or tag appears in the
    search results.
    """
    if not isinstance(response, dict) or response.get("error"):
        return ""
    views, databases, tags = _resources_from_metadata_response(response)
    if not views and not databases and not tags:
        return ""
    try:
        records = []
        for memory_type in LINKED_MEMORY_TYPES:
            records.extend(_load_visible(username, memory_type, agent_id, include_shared_general))
    except MemoryError:
        return ""
    matched = [
        record for record in records
        if _links_match_resources(record.get("links"), views, databases, tags)
    ]
    if not matched:
        return ""
    sections = []
    metadata_lines = [_index_line(record) for record in matched if record.get("type") == "metadata"]
    user_metadata_lines = [_index_line(record) for record in matched if record.get("type") == "user-metadata"]
    if metadata_lines:
        sections.append(
            "<metadata_memories>\n"
            "Metadata memories for these results. Read one with read_memory before applying it.\n"
            + "\n".join(metadata_lines)
            + "\n</metadata_memories>"
        )
    if user_metadata_lines:
        sections.append(
            "<user-metadata_memories>\n"
            "User-metadata memories for these results. Read one with read_memory before applying it.\n"
            + "\n".join(user_metadata_lines)
            + "\n</user-metadata_memories>"
        )
    return "\n\n" + "\n\n".join(sections)

def list_memories(username, memory_type=None, link_kind=None, link_name=None, query=None, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Return this user's memories for one agent, optionally filtered.

    With sharing on, a specialized agent also lists the general agent's
    ``user`` and ``user-metadata`` memories. ``metadata`` memories are listed
    from every agent this user has.
    """
    types = (memory_type,) if memory_type else MEMORY_TYPES
    if memory_type:
        _validate_type(memory_type)
    link_kind = _blank_to_none(link_kind)
    link_name = _blank_to_none(link_name)
    query = _blank_to_none(query)
    if link_kind and link_kind != "none":
        _validate_link_kind(link_kind)
    records = []
    for current_type in types:
        records.extend(_load_visible(username, current_type, agent_id, include_shared_general))
    return [
        record for record in records
        if _matches_filter(record, link_kind, link_name, query)
    ]

def list_metadata_for_resource(link_kind, link_name):
    """Metadata memories every user attached to one view, database, or tag.

    A memory linked to several resources is included when any one of them
    matches. User memories are never included, even when they carry the same link.
    """
    link_kind = _validate_link_kind(link_kind)
    link_name = _validate_link_name(link_kind, link_name)
    ensure_memory_store()
    return [
        _record_from_stored(row)
        for row in UserMemories.list_metadata_for_link(link_kind, link_name)
    ]

def metadata_link_index():
    """Databases, tags, and views that already have a metadata memory.

    A view link ``database.view`` is filed under that database. ``count`` is
    the number of metadata memories linked to that exact resource. One memory
    linked to several resources is counted under each of them. A database is
    included when a view inside it has memories, even if the database itself
    has none. Tags have no nested views, because a memory does not record
    which views carry a tag.
    """
    ensure_memory_store()
    databases = {}
    tags = {}
    views_by_database = {}

    def slot(store, name):
        key = str(name).casefold()
        row = store.get(key)
        if row is None:
            row = {"name": name, "count": 0}
            store[key] = row
        return row

    for kind, name in UserMemories.list_metadata_links():
        if kind == "database":
            slot(databases, name)["count"] += 1
        elif kind == "tag":
            slot(tags, name)["count"] += 1
        elif kind == "view":
            database, _separator, view_name = str(name).partition(".")
            if not database or not view_name:
                continue
            slot(databases, database)
            slot(views_by_database.setdefault(database.casefold(), {}), name)["count"] += 1

    catalog = []
    for key, database in databases.items():
        views = sorted(
            views_by_database.get(key, {}).values(),
            key=lambda item: item["name"].casefold(),
        )
        catalog.append({"name": database["name"], "count": database["count"], "views": views})
    catalog.sort(key=lambda item: item["name"].casefold())
    return {
        "databases": catalog,
        "tags": sorted(tags.values(), key=lambda item: item["name"].casefold()),
    }

def find_memory(username, name, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Return the memory with this name that the agent can see.

    A name is unique for a user, so the caller does not pass a type.
    """
    name = _validate_name(name)
    matches = []
    for memory_type in MEMORY_TYPES:
        for record in _load_visible(username, memory_type, agent_id, include_shared_general):
            if record["name"] == name:
                matches.append(record)
    if not matches:
        raise MemoryError(f"No memory named '{name}'.")
    if len(matches) > 1:
        raise MemoryError(f"More than one memory is named '{name}'.")
    return matches[0]

def read_memory(username, memory_type, name, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Return one memory owned by ``username``, including its markdown.

    Looks in this agent's scope first. With sharing on, a ``user`` or
    ``user-metadata`` memory of the general agent is found too. A
    ``metadata`` memory is found on whichever agent this user saved it.
    """
    memory_type = _validate_type(memory_type)
    name = _validate_name(name)
    records = _load_visible(username, memory_type, agent_id, include_shared_general)
    for record in records:
        if record["name"] == name:
            return record
    raise MemoryError(f"No {memory_type} memory named '{name}'.")

def write_memory(username, memory_type, name, description, body, links=None, allow_create=True, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Create or replace one memory and refresh its index line.

    ``agent_id`` is the scope a ``user`` or ``user-metadata`` memory is
    written to. When sharing is on and this agent has no row of that name,
    the general agent's row is updated instead of saving a second copy.
    This agent's own row still wins when both exist. A second memory with
    the same name is refused, whether the other row has a different type or
    belongs to another agent. A ``metadata`` memory is one fact for this
    user: a write from any agent updates the copy that already exists,
    whichever agent saved it, and drops any other copy of that name.
    ``links`` replaces the whole list. A ``user`` memory takes no links; a
    ``user-metadata`` or ``metadata`` memory needs at least one.
    ``modified`` is always written by the store. A user-memory write that
    crosses the index limit still succeeds; the returned message says so.
    ``allow_create`` is False for the sample chatbot UI, which can edit a
    memory the agent already saved but cannot create one. The agent tools
    leave it True.
    """
    username = _validate_username(username)
    memory_type = _validate_type(memory_type)
    scope_agent = _agent_id(agent_id)
    name = _validate_name(name)
    description = _validate_description(description)
    body = _validate_body(body)
    links = _validate_links(memory_type, links)
    record = {
        "name": name,
        "description": description,
        "type": memory_type,
        "owner": username,
        "agent_id": scope_agent,
        "modified": _now(),
        "links": links,
        "body": body,
        "filename": f"{name}.md",
    }
    ensure_memory_store()
    records = []
    with _user_lock(username):
        target_agent = scope_agent
        extras = []
        if memory_type == "metadata":
            copies = _metadata_named(username, name)
            chosen = _preferred_metadata(copies, scope_agent)
            if chosen is None:
                created = True
            else:
                created = False
                target_agent = chosen.get("agent_id") or scope_agent
                extras = [
                    copy for copy in copies
                    if (copy.get("agent_id") or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID) != target_agent
                ]
        else:
            existing = {
                item["name"]: item
                for item in _load_entries(username, memory_type, scope_agent)
            }
            if name in existing:
                created = False
            else:
                shared = _shared_general_memory(
                    username, memory_type, name, scope_agent, include_shared_general,
                )
                if shared is None:
                    created = True
                else:
                    created = False
                    target_agent = shared.get("agent_id") or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID
        conflict = _name_conflict(username, name, memory_type, target_agent)
        if conflict:
            raise MemoryError(_name_taken_message(conflict, name))
        if created and not allow_create:
            raise MemoryError("Memories can only be created by the agent.")
        record["agent_id"] = target_agent
        record["content"] = _render_file(record)
        stored_body = record["body"]
        if created:
            inserted = UserMemories.insert(
                username,
                target_agent,
                memory_type,
                name,
                description,
                stored_body,
                links,
                username,
                record["modified"],
                UserMemories.next_position(username, target_agent, memory_type),
            )
            if not inserted:
                conflict = _name_conflict(username, name, memory_type, target_agent)
                if conflict:
                    raise MemoryError(_name_taken_message(conflict, name))
                updated = UserMemories.update(
                    username,
                    target_agent,
                    memory_type,
                    name,
                    description,
                    stored_body,
                    links,
                    username,
                    record["modified"],
                )
                if not updated:
                    raise MemoryError(f"No {memory_type} memory named '{name}'.")
        else:
            updated = UserMemories.update(
                username,
                target_agent,
                memory_type,
                name,
                description,
                stored_body,
                links,
                username,
                record["modified"],
            )
            if not updated:
                raise MemoryError(f"No {memory_type} memory named '{name}'.")
        for extra in extras:
            UserMemories.delete(
                username,
                extra.get("agent_id") or GLOBAL_AGENT_ID,
                memory_type,
                name,
            )
        if memory_type == "user":
            records = _load_entries(username, memory_type, scope_agent)
    verb = "Saved" if created else "Updated"
    message = f"{verb} {memory_type} memory '{name}'."
    if memory_type == "user":
        index_text = _index_text(records)
        notice = index_limit_notice("user", index_text)
        if notice:
            if _status_from_text(index_text)["over_limit"]:
                message = f"{message} The write succeeded. {notice}"
            else:
                message = f"{message} {notice}"
    logging.info(f"Memory {verb.lower()} for '{username}' on agent '{target_agent}': {memory_type}/{name}")
    return {
        "record": _public_record(record),
        "created": created,
        "message": message,
        "index": user_index_status(username, scope_agent, include_shared_general),
    }

def delete_memory(username, memory_type, name, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Delete one memory this user owns and its index line.

    ``metadata`` is per user, so every copy of that name is removed, including
    one saved by another agent. ``user`` and ``user-metadata`` remove the row
    this agent can see. Its own row wins when both exist. With sharing on, a
    general-agent row is removed when this agent has no row of its own.
    """
    username = _validate_username(username)
    memory_type = _validate_type(memory_type)
    scope_agent = _agent_id(agent_id)
    name = _validate_name(name)
    ensure_memory_store()
    with _user_lock(username):
        if memory_type == "metadata":
            copies = _metadata_named(username, name)
            if not copies:
                raise MemoryError(f"No {memory_type} memory named '{name}'.")
            removed = False
            for copy in copies:
                if UserMemories.delete(
                    username,
                    copy.get("agent_id") or scope_agent,
                    memory_type,
                    name,
                ):
                    removed = True
            if not removed:
                raise MemoryError(f"No {memory_type} memory named '{name}'.")
        else:
            visible = _load_visible(username, memory_type, scope_agent, include_shared_general)
            match = next((record for record in visible if record["name"] == name), None)
            target = (match.get("agent_id") if match else None) or scope_agent
            if match is None or not UserMemories.delete(username, target, memory_type, name):
                raise MemoryError(f"No {memory_type} memory named '{name}'.")
    message = f"Deleted {memory_type} memory '{name}'."
    notice = ""
    if memory_type == "user":
        notice = index_limit_notice("user", _index_text(_load_visible(username, "user", scope_agent, include_shared_general)))
        if notice:
            message = f"{message} {notice}"
    logging.info(f"Memory deleted for '{username}' on agent '{scope_agent}': {memory_type}/{name}")
    return {"message": message, "index": user_index_status(username, scope_agent, include_shared_general)}

def user_index_status(username, agent_id=GLOBAL_AGENT_ID, include_shared_general=False):
    """Line count for the visible user-memory index, plus limit flags."""
    try:
        text = _index_text(_load_visible(username, "user", agent_id, include_shared_general))
    except MemoryError:
        text = ""
    return _status_from_text(text)

def index_limit_notice(memory_type, index_text):
    """Warning text when a user index is near or over the 200-memory limit."""
    if memory_type != "user":
        return ""
    status = _status_from_text(index_text)
    if status["over_limit"]:
        dropped = status["dropped_lines"]
        notice = (
            f"The user memory index is over its load limit "
            f"({status['lines']} lines; "
            f"only the first {MAX_INDEX_LINES} lines are loaded). "
            "The overflow will be dropped on the next load. "
            "Rewrite the index by merging or dropping stale memories."
        )
        if dropped:
            preview = dropped[:30]
            extra = len(dropped) - len(preview)
            shown = "\n".join(preview)
            notice = f"{notice}\nThese index lines will be dropped on the next load:\n{shown}"
            if extra:
                notice = f"{notice}\n... and {extra} more."
        return notice
    if status["near_limit"]:
        return (
            f"The user memory index is near its load limit "
            f"({status['lines']} lines, the limit is {MAX_INDEX_LINES} lines). "
            "Shorten it by merging or dropping stale memories."
        )
    return ""

def format_index(records):
    """Render index lines for a list of memory records."""
    if not records:
        return ""
    return "\n".join(_index_line(record) for record in records)

def _public_record(record):
    copied = dict(record)
    copied.pop("path", None)
    return copied

def _status_from_text(index_text):
    lines = index_text.splitlines()
    kept, truncated = _truncate_index(index_text)
    over = truncated
    near = (not over) and len(lines) >= NEAR_INDEX_LINES
    return {
        "lines": len(lines),
        "near_limit": near,
        "over_limit": over,
        "dropped_lines": lines[len(kept):],
    }

def _truncate_index(index_text):
    """Keep the leading lines that fit in the 200-line cap."""
    if not index_text:
        return [], False
    all_lines = index_text.splitlines()
    kept = all_lines[:MAX_INDEX_LINES]
    return kept, len(kept) < len(all_lines)

def _inline_graph_reference(tool_call_id):
    if not tool_call_id:
        return ""
    return f"\n\nTo show this graph in your answer, paste this markdown code block exactly where the chart should appear:\n```graph\n{tool_call_id}\n```"

def _knowledge_query_impl(search_query, vector_store, collection, k=5, document_size_limit_chars=10000):
    """
    Search a single collection inside the knowledge base.

    Returns a dict carrying the rendered answer plus collection metadata so the
    UI can show provenance.
    """
    try:
        result = vector_store.search(
            query=search_query,
            k=k,
            scores=False,
            database_names=[collection],
        )

        blocks = [
            f"<result_{i + 1}>\n{doc.page_content[:document_size_limit_chars]}\n</result_{i + 1}>"
            for i, doc in enumerate(result)
        ]
        return {"answer": "\n\n".join(blocks)}
    except Exception as e:
        return {
            "error": f"Knowledge query failed: {e}",
            "traceback": traceback.format_exc(),
        }

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def generate_vql(
    runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext],
    request: str,
    limit: int = 0,
    view_names: list[str] | None = None,
):
    """Takes a precise natural language request, generates a single valid VQL query from it and executes it, returning the query execution result.

    Limitations:
    - This tool cannot handle multi-step workflows. (i.e. do this first, then do that. if this fails, then do that, etc)
    - This tool does not have memory of previous requests or conversations. Every individual request to this tool must be self-contained, meaning it must not rely on recollection of previous requests.

    Args:
        request: The natural language request to generate a single VQL query from. For example, "Generate a VQL query to count the number of loan_id in the view org.loan_status where loan_status is 'active' and date_created is after or equal to 2026-01-01".
        limit: Maximum number of rows to return. If omitted, it defaults to the generate_vql limit configured for this session.
        view_names: Optional list of views (format: database.view_name) to be used in the VQL query, for example ['organization.loans', 'database.loan1']. If you're certain about the views you want the VQL to use, setting this value will speed up the VQL generation process because it won't have to look for relevant views in the database.
    """

    if runtime.context.vdp_database_names:
        logging.info(f"Received UI filters: vdp_database_names={runtime.context.vdp_database_names}")
    if runtime.context.vdp_tag_names:
        logging.info(f"Received UI filters: vdp_tag_names={runtime.context.vdp_tag_names}")

    auth = create_basic_auth_header(runtime.context.username, runtime.context.password)
    default_limit = (runtime.context.ai_sdk_params or {}).get("vql_execute_rows_limit")
    effective_limit = default_limit if limit in (None, 0) else limit

    extra_params = dict(runtime.context.ai_sdk_params or {})
    extra_params.pop("request", None)
    extra_params.pop("view_names", None)
    extra_params.pop("filter_logic", None)

    response = denodo_tools.generate_vql(
        natural_language_query=request,
        api_host=runtime.context.api_host,
        auth=auth,
        vdp_database_names=runtime.context.vdp_database_names,
        vdp_tag_names=runtime.context.vdp_tag_names,
        limit=effective_limit,
        custom_instructions=runtime.context.ai_sdk_custom_instructions,
        view_names=view_names or [],
        verify_ssl=runtime.context.verify_ssl,
        timeout=runtime.context.timeout,
        cancel_event=runtime.context.cancel_event,
        **extra_params,
    )

    return format_generate_vql_output(response)

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def deep_query(
    runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext],
    analysis_request: str,
    languages: list[str] | None = None,
):
    """Launch an advanced DeepQuery analysis on the user's data in Denodo as a BACKGROUND job and return immediately.

    The analysis and the HTML report take minutes and run asynchronously: this tool never returns the analysis
    results, only a confirmation that the job started. The user follows the progress and opens the finished
    reports from the DeepQuery Reports Manager. Never claim the analysis or report is finished, and do not invent findings.

    Args:
        analysis_request: Detailed analysis request to perform.
        languages: Languages to generate the report in, one report per language, for example ['English', 'French']. If the user did not ask for specific languages, pass a single-item list with the language the user is writing in during the conversation (for example ['Spanish']).
    """

    try:
        job_context = ReportJobContext.from_user_context(runtime.context)
        analysis_id, reports = report_job_manager.submit(job_context, analysis_request, languages)
    except ValueError as e:
        return (str(e), {"error": str(e), "status": "rejected"})
    except Exception as e:
        logging.error("Could not start the DeepQuery background job", exc_info=True)
        return (
            f"The DeepQuery background job could not be started: {e}",
            {"error": str(e), "status": "rejected"},
        )

    report_languages = [report["language"] for report in reports]
    report_word = "report" if len(reports) == 1 else "reports"
    content = (
        f"Background job started: {len(reports)} {report_word} queued ({', '.join(report_languages)}). "
        "The analysis is running in the background and is NOT finished. Tell the user they can follow "
        "the progress and open the report from the DeepQuery Reports Manager in the header."
    )
    artifact = {
        "analysis_id": analysis_id,
        "report_ids": [report["report_id"] for report in reports],
        "languages": report_languages,
        "status": "queued",
    }
    return (content, artifact)

                runtime.context.share_general_memory,
            )
        except Exception:
            logging.exception("Failed to attach metadata memories to metadata_search")
    return content, artifact

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def knowledge_query(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], search_query: str, collection: str, k: int = 5):
    """Search a single collection in the user's knowledge base with similarity search.

    Args:
        search_query: Natural language query to search for in the collection.
        collection: REQUIRED. The exact name of the collection to search, taken from the
            list shown in extra_tools_guidance. To cover several collections, call this
            tool once per collection.
        k: Maximum number of results to return (default 5).
    """
    if not runtime.context.vector_store:
        return (
            "Knowledge base is not configured.",
            {"error": "knowledge_base_not_configured"},
        )

    active = runtime.context.active_csv_sources or []
    requested = (collection or "").strip()

    if not requested:
        return (
            "The `collection` argument is required. Pick one of the active collections: "
            f"{', '.join(active) if active else '(none active)'}.",
            {"error": "collection_required", "active_collections": active},
        )

    if not active:
        # No subscribed collections means the user has nothing to search. We
        # MUST refuse — otherwise the LLM could be coaxed into naming someone
        # else's private collection and reading it through the shared store.
        return (
            "You have no collections active for this chatbot. Open the Knowledge "
            "Base Manager to activate one before asking a knowledge-base question.",
            {"error": "no_collections_active", "active_collections": []},
        )

    if requested not in active:
        return (
            f"Collection '{requested}' is not in your active set. "
            f"Active collections: {', '.join(active)}.",
            {"error": "collection_not_active", "active_collections": active},
        )

    collection_description = (runtime.context.kb_collections or {}).get(requested, "")

    response = _knowledge_query_impl(
        search_query=search_query,
        vector_store=runtime.context.vector_store,
        collection=requested,
        k=k,
    )
    response["collection_name"] = requested
    response["collection_description"] = collection_description

    if 'error' in response:
        return (f"Knowledge query failed: {response.get('error', 'Unknown error')}", response)

    content = response.get("answer", "Knowledge query failed, please check the additional information modal.")
    return (content, response)

# Skill Tools
# Skills are reusable guidance the agent reads on demand. System skills live
# on disk and are shared by everyone; personal skills live in the database and
# belong to a single user. Reading and personal skill management are open to
# all users; managing SYSTEM skills requires can_manage_skills.
# =============================================================================

_SKILL_MANAGEMENT_DENIED = (
    "You are not authorized to edit system skills. Only administrators "
    "(or explicitly allowed users/roles) can manage system skills."
)

def _available_skill_or_error(context, skill_name):
    """Return an error message unless skill_name is active in the user's current context.

    Skills that do not apply here — inactive for this user/agent, not declared
    by the agent, or force-disabled by feature flags (e.g. 'deepquery' when
    DeepQuery is off) — must not be readable from the chat, so the agent never
    follows guidance for features it cannot use. Resolved live so skills
    created or activated during the conversation are picked up.
    """
    available = skills.active_skills_for_user(
        context.username,
        context.agent_id,
        context.allowed_system_skills,
        context.disabled_skills,
    )
    if skill_name not in available:
        return (
            f"Skill '{skill_name}' is not available in this context. "
            f"You can only read the skills listed in your system prompt."
        )
    return None

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def read_skill(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], skill_name: str):
    """Read the full instructions (SKILL.md) of a skill, so you can follow its guidance.

    Read the relevant skill BEFORE acting on a task it covers. The system prompt lists
    the available skill names and descriptions.

    Args:
        skill_name: The name of the skill to read. For example, 'deepquery'.
    """
    try:
        error = _available_skill_or_error(runtime.context, skill_name)
        if error:
            return (error, {"error": error, "skill": skill_name})
        content = skills.read_skill_for_user(runtime.context.username, skill_name)
        return (content, {"skill": skill_name})
    except skills.SkillError as e:
        return (str(e), {"error": str(e), "skill": skill_name})

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def read_skill_reference(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], skill_name: str, reference_name: str):
    """Read one of a skill's reference documents for deeper detail on a sub-topic.

    The available reference names for each skill are listed next to the skill in the
    system prompt.

    Args:
        skill_name: The name of the skill. For example, 'deepquery'.
        reference_name: The name of the reference document (without extension). For example, 'interpret_results'.
    """
    try:
        error = _available_skill_or_error(runtime.context, skill_name)
        if error:
            return (error, {"error": error, "skill": skill_name, "reference": reference_name})
        content = skills.read_skill_reference(skill_name, reference_name)
        return (content, {"skill": skill_name, "reference": reference_name})
    except skills.SkillError as e:
        return (str(e), {"error": str(e), "skill": skill_name, "reference": reference_name})

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def edit_skill(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], skill_name: str, text_to_search: str, text_to_replace: str):
    """Edit a skill by replacing text. Personal skills are always editable by their
    owner; editing shared SYSTEM skills requires skill-management permission.

    IMPORTANT: This replaces ALL occurrences of text_to_search with text_to_replace.
    Make text_to_search specific enough to match exactly what you intend to change
    (including whitespace).

    Args:
        skill_name: The name of the skill to edit. For example, 'deepquery'.
        text_to_search: The exact text to find. All occurrences are replaced.
        text_to_replace: The text to replace it with.
    """
    username = runtime.context.username
    try:
        try:
            count = skills.edit_personal_skill(username, skill_name, text_to_search, text_to_replace)
            scope = "personal"
        except skills.PersonalSkillNotFoundError:
            # Not one of the user's personal skills: fall back to system skills.
            if not runtime.context.can_manage_skills:
                return (_SKILL_MANAGEMENT_DENIED, {"error": "unauthorized", "skill": skill_name})
            count = skills.edit_skill(skill_name, text_to_search, text_to_replace)
            scope = "system"
        return (
            f"Replaced {count} occurrence(s) in {scope} skill '{skill_name}'.",
            {"skill": skill_name, "scope": scope, "replacements": count},
        )
    except skills.SkillError as e:
        return (str(e), {"error": str(e), "skill": skill_name})

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def edit_skill_reference(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], skill_name: str, reference_name: str, text_to_search: str, text_to_replace: str):
    """Edit a skill reference document by replacing text. Requires skill-management permission.

    IMPORTANT: This replaces ALL occurrences of text_to_search with text_to_replace.
    Make text_to_search specific enough to match exactly what you intend to change
    (including whitespace).

    Args:
        skill_name: The name of the skill. For example, 'deepquery'.
        reference_name: The name of the reference document (without extension). For example, 'interpret_results'.
        text_to_search: The exact text to find. All occurrences are replaced.
        text_to_replace: The text to replace it with.
    """
    if not runtime.context.can_manage_skills:
        return (_SKILL_MANAGEMENT_DENIED, {"error": "unauthorized", "skill": skill_name})
    try:
        count = skills.edit_skill_reference(skill_name, reference_name, text_to_search, text_to_replace)
        return (
            f"Replaced {count} occurrence(s) in reference '{reference_name}' of skill '{skill_name}'.",
            {"skill": skill_name, "reference": reference_name, "replacements": count},

    except skills.SkillError as e:
        return (str(e), {"error": str(e), "skill": skill_name, "reference": reference_name})

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def create_skill(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], skill_name: str, content: str):
    """Create a brand new PERSONAL skill for this user, only visible to them.

    The content must be the full markdown body of the skill, starting with a
    YAML frontmatter block containing a 'name' and a 'description'.
    Name: max 64 characters, lowercase letters/numbers/hyphens only, must not
    start or end with a hyphen. Description: non-empty, max 1024 characters.

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def create_skill_reference(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], skill_name: str, reference_name: str, content: str):
    """Create a new reference document inside an existing skill. Requires skill-management permission.

        skill_name: The name of the existing skill the reference belongs to. For example, 'deepquery'.

# Memory Tools
# =============================================================================

def _memory_scope(runtime):
    context = runtime.context
    return (
        context.agent_id or "global",
        context.share_general_memory,
    )

def _memory_call(action):
    try:
        return action()
    except memory.MemoryError as exc:
        return (str(exc), {"error": str(exc)})

def _stored_index_text(records):
    rendered = memory.format_index(records)
    if not rendered:
        return ""
    return f"{rendered}\n"

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def read_memory(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], name: str):
    """Read a specific memory's contents.

    The name is unique for this user, so the type is not needed.

    Args:
        name: Memory name, without the .md extension. For example, 'prefers-eur'.
    """
    def _read():
        agent_id, share_general = _memory_scope(runtime)
        record = memory.find_memory(runtime.context.username, name, agent_id, share_general)
        return (record.get("content") or record.get("body") or "", record)
    return _memory_call(_read)

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def list_memories(
    runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext],
    memory_type: str = "",
    link_kind: str = "",
    link_name: str = "",
):
    """List memory index lines for this user on this agent.

    Use this to see 'user-metadata' or 'metadata' memories, or 'user'
    memories that fell past the portion of the index loaded into the
    system prompt. Leave a filter empty when you do not want to apply it.

    Args:
        memory_type: 'user', 'user-metadata', 'metadata', or empty for all.
        link_kind: Optional filter: 'view', 'database', 'tag', or 'none'.
            A memory matches when any of its links has this kind.
        link_name: Optional link name. For a view, use database.view_name.
            A memory matches when any of its links has this name.
    """
    def _list():
        agent_id, share_general = _memory_scope(runtime)
        records = memory.list_memories(
            runtime.context.username,
            memory_type=memory_type or None,
            link_kind=link_kind,
            link_name=link_name,
            agent_id=agent_id,
            include_shared_general=share_general,
        )
        content = memory.format_index(records) or "No memories match."
        if not memory_type or memory_type == "user":
            user_records = memory.list_memories(
                runtime.context.username, memory_type="user",
                agent_id=agent_id, include_shared_general=share_general,
            )
            notice = memory.index_limit_notice("user", _stored_index_text(user_records))
            if notice:
                content = f"{content}\n\n{notice}"
        return (content, {"memories": records})
    return _memory_call(_list)

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def write_memory(
    runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext],
    memory_type: str,
    name: str,
    description: str,
    body: str,
    links: str = "",
):
    """Save or replace a memory for this user.

    Pick the memory type by what it represents:
    - 'user': a fact or preference about the person, with no link to any specific metadata. For
      example, a personal preference: that they like to be called Jamie instead of James or
      a workflow preference that applies always: James likes to show all currency fields converted to EUR.
    - 'user-metadata': a personal preference about specific metadata. It
      must be linked to at least one view, database, or tag. For example,
      that Jamie likes salary in samples_bank.loan to show the currency
      sign. The same preference with no link belongs in 'user'.
    - 'metadata': an objective fact about the metadata that the metadata
      itself does not say, linked to at least one view, database, or tag.
      For example, that the currency of salary in samples_bank.loan is USD.
      The logic is that a 'metadata' memory is a fact that is applicable to any user, not just the one you are talking to.

    One linked memory can be linked to several views, databases, and tags.
    Pass every link the memory should keep.

    Name: max 64 characters, lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, and it
    must not start or end with a hyphen.

    Args:
        memory_type: 'user', 'user-metadata', or 'metadata'.
        name: Filename stem. For example, 'revenue-means-net'.
        description: One-line title shown in the memory index.
        body: The note to reuse later. State the fact plainly.
        links: One link per line, as kind:name. kind is view, database, or tag.
            A view name is database.view_name. Example:
            view:sales.orders
            view:finance.invoices
            database:sales
            tag:revenue
            Leave empty for a 'user' memory; required otherwise.
    """
    def _write():
        agent_id, share_general = _memory_scope(runtime)
        result = memory.write_memory(
            runtime.context.username,
            memory_type,
            name,
            description,
            body,
            links=links,
            agent_id=agent_id,
            include_shared_general=share_general,
        )
        return (result["message"], result)
    return _memory_call(_write)

@tool(response_format="content_and_artifact")
def delete_memory(runtime: ToolRuntime[UserContext], name: str):
    """Delete one memory this user owns.

    The name is unique for this user, so the type is not needed.

    Args:
        name: Memory name, without the .md extension. For example, 'prefers-eur'.
    """
    def _delete():
        agent_id, share_general = _memory_scope(runtime)
        record = memory.find_memory(runtime.context.username, name, agent_id, share_general)
        result = memory.delete_memory(
            runtime.context.username, record["type"], name, agent_id, share_general,
        )
        return (result["message"], result)
    return _memory_call(_delete)

import logging

from flask_login import login_user, logout_user, login_required, current_user

from sample_chatbot.config import get_config, get_agents_metadata_by_user
from sample_chatbot.services.agent_prerequisites import missing_agent_prerequisites, missing_prerequisites_message
from sample_chatbot.services.ui_preferences import apply_agent, apply_profile
from sample_chatbot.services.user_store import user_store
from sample_chatbot.utils.ai_sdk_client import (
    get_user_access_info,
    get_synced_resources,
    get_ai_sdk_info,
    filter_synced_resources,
    filter_partial_resources
)

auth_bp = Blueprint('auth', __name__)

@auth_bp.route("/api/login", methods=["POST"])
def login():
    """Authenticate user and create session."""
    config = get_config()
    data = request.json
    username = data.get('username')
    password = data.get('password')

    if not username or not password:
        return jsonify({"success": False, "message": "Username and password are required"}), 400

    status, access_info = get_user_access_info(
        api_host=config.ai_sdk_host,
        username=username,
        password=password,
        verify_ssl=config.ai_sdk_verify_ssl
    )

    if status != 200:
        return jsonify({"success": False, "message": access_info}), status

    roles = access_info.get("roles", [])
    is_admin = access_info.get("is_admin", False)
    legacy_permissions_endpoint = access_info.get("legacy_permissions_endpoint", False)

    synced_resources, partial_resources, user_sync_permissions = get_synced_resources(
        api_host=config.ai_sdk_host,
        username=username,
        password=password,
        verify_ssl=config.ai_sdk_verify_ssl
    )

    ai_sdk_info = get_ai_sdk_info(
        api_host=config.ai_sdk_host,
        username=username,
        password=password,
        verify_ssl=config.ai_sdk_verify_ssl
    )

    user = user_store.create_user(username, password, config)
    user.synced_resources = synced_resources
    user.partial_resources = partial_resources
    user.ai_sdk_info = ai_sdk_info
    user.apply_ai_sdk_defaults()
    user.user_sync_permissions = user_sync_permissions
    user.thread_id = str(username)
    user.roles = roles
    user.is_admin = is_admin
    user.legacy_permissions_endpoint = legacy_permissions_endpoint

    profile = apply_profile(user)
    apply_agent(user, user.agent_id)

    login_user(user)
    logging.info(f"[Auth] Login successful for user: {username} | Roles: {roles} | Global admin: {is_admin} | Legacy DM: {legacy_permissions_endpoint}")

    can_use_deepquery = ai_sdk_info.get("can_use_deepquery", True) if ai_sdk_info else True

    return jsonify({
        "success": True,
        "syncedResources": synced_resources,
        "partialResources": partial_resources,
        "userSyncPermissions": user_sync_permissions,
        "globalEnabled": True,
        "agents": get_agents_metadata_by_user(username, roles=roles, is_admin=is_admin, legacy_permissions_endpoint=legacy_permissions_endpoint),
        "config": {
            "can_edit_instructions": config.user_edit_instructions,
            "chatbot_feedback": config.feedback_enabled,
            # Whether KB querying is available on this agent: agent-declared
            # collections work for everyone; otherwise the user needs
            # unstructured-mode permission for their own private collections.
            "unstructured_mode": bool(config.knowledge_bases) or config.is_unstructured_mode_allowed_for_user(
                username=username,
                roles=roles,
                is_admin=is_admin,

    data = request.json
    agent_id = data.get('id')
    active_csvs = data.get('active_csvs')

    agent_config = get_config(agent_id)

    if not agent_config.is_user_allowed(
        username=current_user.id,
        roles=current_user.roles,
        is_admin=current_user.is_admin,
        legacy_permissions_endpoint=current_user.legacy_permissions_endpoint
    ):
        return jsonify({"success": False, "message": "User is not allowed to use this agent"}), 403

    # Declared skills / knowledge bases must exist before the agent can be used.
    missing = missing_agent_prerequisites(agent_config)
    if any(missing.values()):
        logging.warning(f"[Auth] Agent '{agent_config.id}' rejected for '{current_user.id}': missing prerequisites {missing}")

        current_user.set_agent_config(agent_config)
        current_user.thread_id = str(current_user.id) + '-' + str(agent_config.id)

    apply_profile(current_user)
    apply_agent(current_user, agent_config.id)

import logging

from flask import Blueprint, request, jsonify
from flask_login import login_required, current_user

from sample_chatbot.config import get_config
from sample_chatbot.utils.ai_sdk_client import connect_to_ai_sdk, get_synced_resources

metadata_bp = Blueprint('metadata', __name__)

def _refresh_user_synced_resources(config, user):
    """Reload synced/partial resource lists from the AI SDK and drop the cached chatbot."""
    synced_resources, partial_resources, user_sync_permissions = get_synced_resources(
        api_host=config.ai_sdk_host,
        username=user.id,
        password=user.password,
        verify_ssl=config.ai_sdk_verify_ssl
    )
    user.synced_resources = synced_resources
    user.partial_resources = partial_resources
    user.user_sync_permissions = user_sync_permissions
    user.chatbot = None

    return synced_resources, partial_resources

def _get_sync_credentials(config):
    """Get the credentials to use for metadata sync/delete operations.
    Uses AI SDK credentials if configured, otherwise falls back to the logged-in user's credentials."""
    if config.has_ai_sdk_credentials:
        return config.ai_sdk_username, config.ai_sdk_password
    return current_user.id, current_user.password

@metadata_bp.route("/api/delete_metadata", methods=["DELETE"])
@login_required
def delete_metadata():
    """Delete metadata from the AI SDK."""
    config = get_config()

    if not config.allow_sync:
        return jsonify({
            "success": False,
            "message": "Vector DB synchronization is disabled."
        }), 403

    data = request.json
    vdp_database_names = data.get('vdp_database_names', [])
    vdp_tag_names = data.get('vdp_tag_names', [])
    delete_conflicting = data.get('delete_conflicting', False)

    if not vdp_database_names and not vdp_tag_names:
        return jsonify({
            "success": False,
            "message": "At least one database or tag must be provided for deletion."
        }), 400

    try:
        username, password = _get_sync_credentials(config)
        auth = (username, password)
        payload = {
            "vdp_database_names": vdp_database_names,
            "vdp_tag_names": vdp_tag_names,
            "delete_conflicting": delete_conflicting
        }

        response = requests.delete(
            f"{config.ai_sdk_host}/deleteMetadata",
            params=payload,
            auth=auth,
            verify=config.ai_sdk_verify_ssl,
            timeout=300
        )

        if response.status_code == 200:
            synced_resources, partial_resources = _refresh_user_synced_resources(
                config, current_user
            )

            return jsonify({
                "success": True,
                "message": response.json().get('message', 'Deletion successful.'),
                "syncedResources": synced_resources,
                "partialResources": partial_resources
            }), 200

        elif response.status_code == 204:
            from flask import Response
            return Response(status=204)
        else:
            error_message = response.json().get('detail', 'An unknown error occurred during deletion.')
            return jsonify({"success": False, "message": error_message}), response.status_code

    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        logging.error(f"Error calling deleteMetadata endpoint: {str(e)}")
        return jsonify({"success": False, "message": f"Failed to connect to AI SDK: {str(e)}"}), 500

@metadata_bp.route("/api/sync_vdbs", methods=["POST"])
@login_required
def sync_vdbs():
    """Synchronize VDBs with the AI SDK."""
    config = get_config()

    if not config.allow_sync:
        return jsonify({
            "success": False,
            "message": "Vector DB synchronization is disabled."
        }), 403

    vdbs_to_sync = request.json.get('vdbs', [])
    tags_to_sync = request.json.get('tags', [])
    tags_to_ignore = request.json.get('tags_to_ignore', [])
    examples_per_table = request.json.get('examples_per_table', 100)
    incremental = request.json.get('incremental', True)
    parallel = request.json.get('parallel', True)
    timeout_seconds = request.json.get('timeout_seconds', 300)
    embeddings_token_limit = request.json.get('embeddings_token_limit', 0)

    username, password = _get_sync_credentials(config)

    status, result = connect_to_ai_sdk(
        api_host=config.ai_sdk_host,
        username=username,
        password=password,
        insert=True,
        examples_per_table=examples_per_table,
        incremental=incremental,
        parallel=parallel,
        vdp_database_names=vdbs_to_sync,
        vdp_tag_names=tags_to_sync,
        tags_to_ignore=tags_to_ignore,
        verify_ssl=config.ai_sdk_verify_ssl,
        timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
        embeddings_token_limit=embeddings_token_limit
    )

    if status == 200:
        data_usage_errors = result.get("data_usage_errors", [])

        synced_resources, partial_resources = _refresh_user_synced_resources(
            config, current_user
        )

        # Build success message
        message_suffix_parts = []

        if vdbs_to_sync:
            db_label = "database" if len(vdbs_to_sync) == 1 else "databases"
            message_suffix_parts.append(f"{db_label} {', '.join(vdbs_to_sync)}")

        if tags_to_sync:
            tag_label = "tag" if len(tags_to_sync) == 1 else "tags"
            message_suffix_parts.append(f"{tag_label} {', '.join(tags_to_sync)}")

        message_suffix = " and ".join(message_suffix_parts)

        success_message = (
            f"Metadata associated with {message_suffix} successfully synchronized."
            if message_suffix else "Metadata successfully synchronized."
        )

        timings = result.get("timings", {})
        return jsonify({
            "success": True,
            "message": success_message,
            "syncedResources": synced_resources,
            "partialResources": partial_resources,
            "dataUsageErrors": data_usage_errors,
            "timings": timings,
        }), status

    elif status == 204:
        return jsonify({
            "success": True,
            "message": result if result else "Synchronization successful (No Content)"
        }), status
    else:
        return jsonify({"success": False, "message": result}), status

"""
Contains request/response middleware for the chatbot.

import os

from utils.runtime_config import sync_runtime_config

# Applied to every chatbot response. Each entry is (header, env override, default).
# An empty environment value omits that header.
_SECURITY_HEADER_DEFAULTS = (
    (
        'Strict-Transport-Security',
        'CHATBOT_STRICT_TRANSPORT_SECURITY',
        'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains',
    ),
    (
        'Content-Security-Policy',
        'CHATBOT_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY',
        "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; "
        "img-src 'self' data: blob:; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; "
        "worker-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; "
        "form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'",
    ),
    (
        'Permissions-Policy',
        'CHATBOT_PERMISSIONS_POLICY',
        'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()',
    ),
    (
        'X-Content-Type-Options',
        'CHATBOT_X_CONTENT_TYPE_OPTIONS',
        'nosniff',
    ),
)


def security_response_headers():
    """Resolve the security headers for a chatbot response."""
    headers = {}
    for name, env_name, default in _SECURITY_HEADER_DEFAULTS:
        value = os.getenv(env_name, default)
        if value is None:
            continue
        value = value.strip()
        if value:
            headers[name] = value
    return headers


def register_security_headers(app):
    """Add the chatbot security headers to every response."""
    
    headers_to_apply = security_response_headers()

    @app.after_request
    def add_security_headers(response):
        for name, value in headers_to_apply.items():
            response.headers[name] = value
        return response

def register_middleware(blueprint):
    """
    Register middleware on a blueprint.

    Args:
        blueprint: Flask Blueprint instance
    """

    @blueprint.before_request
    def set_logging_context():
        """Set transaction ID and username for the request context."""
        sync_runtime_config()

        transaction_id_var.set(generate_transaction_id())
        username = "anonymous"

        if current_user and current_user.is_authenticated:
            username = current_user.id

        elif request.path.endswith('/login') and request.is_json:
            data = request.json or {}
            if data.get('username'):
                username = data.get('username')

        username_var.set(username)

    @blueprint.after_request
    def add_transaction_id_after_request(response):
        """Add the transaction ID to the response headers."""
        response.headers['X-Transaction-ID'] = transaction_id_var.get()
        return response
